claims.statement: RAD-140 (Testolone) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) and anabolic agent, confirmed as such by the primary discovery/characterization literature; supplier data report high in vitro binding affinity for the androgen receptor (Ki = 7 nM), selective over the progesterone, estrogen, and glucocorticoid receptors, though this specific Ki figure has not been independently confirmed against the primary pharmacology paper's full text. It is a research chemical, not an approved or licensed pharmaceutical.

extractedEvidence.quote: RAD140 is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM; Ki = 7 nM) and anabolic agent.
It is selective for the androgen receptor over the progesterone, estrogen, and glucocorticoid receptors.
WARNING This product is not for human or veterinary use.
This report describes the discovery of RAD140, a potent, orally bioavailable, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM).

reviewFlags: Re-fetched 2026-08-29: PubMed abstract (PMID 24900290, Miller et al., the original RAD140 discovery/characterization paper) independently confirms RAD140's identity as a nonsteroidal SARM, corroborating this claim from primary pharmacology literature rather than a vendor page alone.

The specific Ki = 7 nM binding-affinity figure and receptor-selectivity data could not be confirmed against that paper's full text (paywalled abstract only) in this pass; that figure remains sourced only to the Cayman Chemical vendor page and is labeled as supplier-reported in the statement.
Vendor 'not for human use' language reflects RUO labeling, not a clinical safety determination.

claims.statement: A published case report describes idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury in a 26-year-old male following self-administered RAD140 (Testolone) use, presenting with nausea, vomiting, severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and jaundice (ALT 243 IU/L, total bilirubin 4.9 mg/dL); liver function normalized within 2 months after RAD140 was stopped, without recurrence of symptoms.

context.doseText: Exact dose not determinable from the case report; the patient used a liquid dropper formulation the authors note makes accurate dosing difficult (case-report context, not a use recommendation).

Corrected 2026-08-29: a prior reviewFlag on this claim mischaracterized a re-fetch of the FDA warning letter (already one of this claim's own sourceRefs) as 'independent corroboration'; re-reading the original source does not resolve a review item and that entry has been removed.

Independent corroboration added 2026-08-29 from a genuinely different source family: the Ochsner Journal (2022) documents a separate, unrelated 24-year-old male patient with RAD-140-induced cholestatic liver injury (peak total bilirubin 38.5 mg/dL) who fully recovered after stopping the drug, matching this case report's pattern without being the same source. NCBI LiverTox (structured clinical-toxicology database) independently characterizes SARM/RAD-140 hepatotoxicity as bland, self-limited cholestatic injury, consistent with both cases' outcomes.

claims.statement: RAD140 was evaluated in a completed Phase 1, first-in-human, multi-part clinical trial (NCT03088527) in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer, supplied as an oral drug-in-capsule formulation, with the stated primary purpose of evaluating clinical safety profile, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics; this is an investigational oncology trial, not evidence of an approved indication or of any performance/physique benefit.

context.useCase: investigational oncology trial (safety/tolerability/PK), not an approved indication
context.doseText: Part A dose escalation, Part B safety expansion at the maximum tolerated dose (trial protocol description; not a use recommendation).

claims.statement: RAD-140/Testolone is marketed online with claims that it 'carries the benefits of Testosterone injections without all the risks' and 'reduces fat and increases muscle mass,' packaged with suggested bodybuilding cycle lengths and daily dosing; these efficacy and safety claims are not supported by the human evidence located, which consists of a small single-arm oncology Phase 1 safety/PK trial and isolated case reports of serious adverse effects including liver injury - not controlled trials establishing benefit or safety for muscle-building or performance use.
